claims.text: The initial material is cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy.
The intervention applies a 10 μm thick Al2O3 ceramic coating to the alloy surface.
The coated alloy is intended to operate in an oxidizing atmosphere at temperatures up to 1000 °C.
The coating is intended to remain effective for exposures up to 100 hours.
An exposure of 100 hours is sufficient to assess long-term oxidation behavior.
The Al2O3 coating acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
Restricting oxygen diffusion reduces oxide-scale formation by limiting direct contact between the alloy and the oxidizing atmosphere.
Reduced oxidation limits oxide-induced cracking and embrittlement.
Limiting oxide-induced cracking and embrittlement minimizes degradation of the alloy's mechanical properties.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr develops a 50 μm oxide scale under the specified conditions.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 400 MPa at 1000 °C under the relevant test conditions.
The coating will reduce oxide-scale thickness by 30%, from 50 μm to 35 μm, relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The coating will increase yield strength at 1000 °C by 20%, from 400 MPa to 480 MPa, relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
Applying the coating will improve high-temperature oxygen resistance without sacrificing mechanical performance.
